attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: This says what revenue would be needed to pay the investment off, tied to 'next year'. The payoff goal, the best-case $70B premise and the per-company $100B threshold are all kept. It does not predict that any company will actually reach that revenue.

contract.note: Reading 'next year' as the twelve months to May 19, 2027, and revenue as realized rather than run rate, is a fair, ordinary reading supported by the context. But 'pay this off' has no stated recovery method, so the result depends on how payoff is defined.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own pre-horizon figure: a $37B annualized AI run rate for one company. It is not realized revenue and not a recovery account, so it cannot settle the necessity claim.

reviews.rationale: The horizon ends May 19, 2027, after the evaluation date, and no conclusive early-resolution event is in the packet. It is unknown whether the premises hold (the $900B baseline and $70B combined revenue). No recovery account establishes or refutes the $100B-each threshold. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: Context makes clear that 'both of these companies' means Anthropic and OpenAI. This is a present-tense observation that both lose billions.

contract.note: Reading 'lose billions' as at least $2B in calendar-2025 net losses for each company is a fair, ordinary plain reading. The result is the same on operating losses.

evidence.note: Reuters, via Ynet, reporting on the prospectus: Anthropic's 2025 net loss was nearly $42B and its operating loss about $8B. Both are well above $2B.
Reports audited statements: OpenAI's 2025 net loss was nearly $39B, or about $8B excluding a one-off charge. Its operating loss was about $21B. Above the threshold on any basis.
Anthropic's own S-1 filing gives a $42.0B net loss for 2025. That corroborates e1, but it is on a GAAP basis, not the contract's estimate basis, and it is a company disclosure.

reviews.rationale: Independent reporting shows each company had 2025 net losses far above $2B: about $42B for Anthropic and $39B for OpenAI. Each still lost billions after removing the noncash financing charges. Supported.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words describing his own forthcoming series.

semantics.note: Saying there are factors that 'will cause the AI bubble to finally pop' commits him, without hedging, to an eventual pop. 'This week' is about when he publishes, not a deadline for the pop.

contract.note: Reading 'pop' as a broad, sustained collapse is ordinary. The contract rightly says continued investment cannot disprove a forecast with no deadline.

evidence.note: Crunchbase's Q3 2026 data shows robust AI funding. It weighs against a collapse having happened yet, but cannot refute an eventual one.
Anthropic's own announcement of expanded compute after the post. One company's news is not a sector-wide measure.
Musk warns of a neocloud shakeout and tight debt markets. This shows stress and a prediction, not an established broad collapse.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The packet shows continued AI funding alongside some financing stress, but nothing shows a broad, sustained collapse that would meet the early-resolution rule. Absence of a pop so far is not failure. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: Two factual parts: Meta plans at least $125B of capex in 2026, and Meta has not shown real growth in AI revenue. His dismissal of conversion gains as evidence is reflected in the contract. The opening 'no idea how' is rhetorical.

contract.note: The contract is fair, but 'revenue from AI' is undefined. Whether AI-glasses sales or AI-assisted ad revenue count decides the result, and the speaker gave no definition.

evidence.note: Meta's 10-Q gives 2026 capex guidance of $125-145B, so the lower bound meets the 'at least $125B' part. It says nothing on the revenue part.
Meta's own statement of 'strong growth' in AI glasses sales, with no amount and no isolation of AI's contribution. It is relevant but does not settle AI-attributable revenue growth.

reviews.rationale: The capex part holds: guidance of $125-145B. The central revenue part is not settled. Meta reports growing AI-glasses sales but no isolated AI revenue series, and a missing disclosure line neither proves nor disproves growth. Overall unresolved.
